items.title: Could declining bus service undermine Peel's new LRT?
items.summary: Success of the coming Hazel McCallion LRT line depends on the efficiency of existing bus services, says advocate. The Hazel McCallion LRT is anticipated to be open for public use by 2028. Christian Parisé, a Mississauga resident and local public transit advocate, developed an appreciation for the importance of reliable and efficient public transportation at an early age, often accompanying his grandmother, who did not drive, on trips across the city’s transit system. “As a child I loved getting to go on the bus and subway, it was a fantastic experience. I really didn’t start experiencing transit in a negative way until I started relying on it in high school,” said Parisé. Today, Christian Parisé and Sylvia Menezes Roberts, two local transit advocates from Mississauga and Brampton, fear service changes could have a ripple effect and undermine the success of the upcoming Hazel McCallion Light Rail Transit (LRT) line, expected to begin operating in 2028. Thousands of residents in Mississauga and Brampton rely on public transit services provided by MiWay and Brampton Transit, the municipalities’ respective transit agencies. However, some local advocates in both cities warn that despite millions of dollars being invested in transit expansion, the systems could be heading toward a troubling downward spiral. Recently, both municipalities have recorded declines in public transit ridership. MiWay reported a 10 per cent decrease in passenger boardings in 2025 compared with the previous year, alongside a $9 million drop in revenue. 7-million revenue shortfall. In response to declining ridership, both cities have made service adjustments to varying degrees. In April 2026 alone, Brampton Transit suspended four bus routes, citing low ridership demand, while MiWay adjusted service frequency across several routes, increasing service in some areas while decreasing it in others.

items.title: Alvin Tedjo transition team: Who is advising the new mayor of Mississauga?
items.summary: Tedjo’s 17-member advisory team of developers, politicians and community leaders is helping him prepare to take office as Mississauga’s new mayor on Nov. 16. Mississauga Mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo addressed supporters at his election night party at Wildflower Kitchen and Event Space. He announced a transition team on Oct. 29 Mississauga mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo will be sworn in — along with the rest of the newly elected Mississauga councillors — on Monday, Nov. 16. In preparation Tedjo has put together a transition team of 17 people — developers, community representatives and members of provincial and federal governments representing Mississauga — which met for the first time Nov. 5. In a phone interview with Mississauga News, Tedjo described the team as an advisory body with no decision-making authority, made up of people from across different sectors of the city. “It’s a body that is providing advice to me as the mayor and our new team that we’re bringing in at city hall,” he said. “There’s no payment whatsoever. ” Tedjo said he wanted a cross-section of people with experience across different sectors of the city, including the non-governmental and social services sectors. The 17-member team is chaired by Jodi Robillos, a former commissioner of community services for the City of Mississauga.

items.title: Honouring road traffic victims and supporting safer streets
items.summary: The City of Mississauga remembers those lost or injured in traffic collisions. On Sunday, November 15, the City of Mississauga will join communities around the world in recognizing World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims. The day also honours their families, friends, emergency responders and community members affected by these tragedies. 16 million people die each year because of traffic collisions. Road traffic injuries are also the leading cause of death for children and young adults between the ages of five and 29. More than half of all road traffic deaths are among vulnerable road users, including pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists. That’s why safe streets matter and why communities must continue working to protect everyone. The effects of traffic collisions go far beyond the people directly involved. Family members, friends, witnesses and first responders live with the impact long after a collision happens. The day offers an opportunity to acknowledge this and reflect on the importance of road safety. The City acknowledges that one death on Mississauga roads is one too many. Through its Vision Zero Action Plan, the City continues to work toward eliminating fatal and serious injury collisions. These efforts support safer travel for everyone, whether they’re walking, cycling, taking transit, driving or using mobility devices. Throughout 2026, the City continued investing in programs and infrastructure designed to improve safety and reduce the risk of serious collisions on local roads.

items.title: Cost of Living Takes Centre Stage as Peel's Mayors Press New Chair Ahead of Budget
items.summary: According to insauga.com, the mayors of Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon issued a joint statement urging Peel's newly reappointed regional chair to prioritize affordability in the region's next budget. The outlet reported Mayor Alvin Tedjo joined Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown and Caledon Mayor Christina Early in congratulating Chair Nando Iannicca on his reappointment while pressing him on cost of living concerns. Housing, groceries and other essentials continue to strain household budgets, the mayors said. Iannicca now holds expanded powers under Ontario's Better Regional Governance Act, 2026, insauga.com noted, including the ability to propose the regional budget and introduce amendments during the year. The outlet reported the chair holds veto power over certain council amendments. The mayors said they look forward to seeing what Iannicca and the province table to ease costs.

items.title: Falconer Drive Sewer Rehab Could Slow Streetsville Traffic to One Lane Through Year-End
items.summary: Peel Region crews are rehabilitating the sanitary sewer along Falconer Drive in Mississauga's Streetsville area, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported work began in October and is expected to continue until close to the end of the year, though the timeline could shift due to weather or other unexpected events. Project officials said crews will clean the sewer pipe and install a new resin lining inside it to extend its lifespan. The region said construction is scheduled Monday to Friday to help shorten the overall work period. Insauga.com reported that traffic on the busy street may be temporarily reduced to a single lane while the work is underway.

items.title: Mississauga Trucker Isik Altinisik Wins Truck Hero Award for Highway 401 Rescue
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga truck driver Isik Altinisik has won the Ontario Trucking Association-Bridgestone Truck Hero Award for pulling a woman from a burning vehicle during a massive highway pileup. The outlet reported Altinisik was delivering fresh food to Ottawa on Jan. 27 when he came upon a chain-reaction crash involving about 50 vehicles on Highway 401 near Trenton amid whiteout conditions, including a 17-vehicle pileup. Rather than driving on, he rushed toward the wreckage to help trapped motorists, insauga.com said. Among them was Theresa Rozendaal, whose SUV had caught fire with flames emerging from the hood and the windshield shattered, according to the report. Altinisik broke the rear window with his bare hands, injuring himself, before pulling Rozendaal from the vehicle and getting her to safety, insauga.com reported.

items.title: G.E. Booth Plant Odours to Drop More Than 90 Percent by 2027, Peel Region Says
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Peel Region says foul odours that have affected southeast Mississauga residents for decades near the G.E. Booth Water Resource Recovery Facility will nearly disappear once the 71-year-old plant is modernized. The outlet reported the region expects odours to drop by more than 90 per cent once the upgrade work is finished, with completion on track for 2027. About half of the odour mitigation program is scheduled to be done by the end of 2026, with most remaining work finished the following year, insauga.com said. The upgrades are meant to keep pace with growth, including the roughly 16,000 new homes planned for the nearby Lakeview Village development, according to the report. The facility, formerly the Lakeview Wastewater Treatment Plant, is Peel's largest and serves east Mississauga, east Brampton and part of York Region, insauga.com noted.

items.title: Cricket Advocate Ranil Mendis Named Mississauga's 2026 Citizen of the Year
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, cricket advocate and philanthropist Ranil Mendis has been named Mississauga's 2026 citizen of the year. The outlet reported Mendis received the Gordon S. Shipp Memorial Award for Citizen of the Year from Deputy Mayor Matt Mahoney on Nov. 4 at the city's annual Civic Recognition awards event. Mississauga.com said Mendis was recognized for his leadership, community service, philanthropy and ability to inspire others, according to a city news release. Mahoney said in the release that Mississauga is a great city because of people like Mendis who give back, the outlet reported. A board member with the Ontario School Cricket Association, Mendis helped bring the Mayor's School Cricket Program to Mississauga and the Chartered Institute of Management Accountants Schools Cricket Program to several Ontario school boards, according to Mississauga.com.

items.title: El Niño to bring milder temperatures, and more potholes, to Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga officials say a potentially historic El Niño that’s expected to bring milder temperatures to southern Ontario this fall and winter will also impact the city in other ways. Coupled with climate change, “which is warming ocean waters,” the El Niño effect could be even stronger, the City of Mississauga said this week. “In Mississauga, that could mean a slower start to winter and more days when temperatures rise above and fall below freezing,” city officials said Thursday, adding some city services “may be delayed or look different than usual” as a result. “A strong El Niño could bring a longer, milder fall and a higher chance of extreme weather to Mississauga,” the city continued. Beyond Mississauga and southern Ontario, weather experts have said El Niño, a natural weather pattern caused by warmer-than-normal ocean temperatures that can affect global weather, will also have a strong impact across much of Canada in the coming months. ” Residents should become familiar with the municipality’s online emergency preparedness guide, officials added.

items.title: Jamal Francique Inquest Delayed to Friday, Nearly Seven Years After Mississauga Police Shooting
items.summary: According to insauga.com, the coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique has been postponed by a day and will now begin Friday instead of Thursday. The outlet reported a notice on the inquest's website said further details on the delay would be provided then. Francique died in hospital on Jan. 9, 2020, two days after Peel Regional Police shot him during an attempted arrest in Mississauga; he was 28, insauga.com said. Ontario's Special Investigations Unit cleared the officers of wrongdoing about a year later, saying the officer who fired reported fearing for his life after Francique drove toward him, according to the report. The SIU noted it still had questions about the officer's decision to position himself near the fleeing vehicle, insauga.com noted.

items.title: Update: Wanted Suspect Arrested in Mississauga Shooting
items.summary: Region of Peel – Investigators from the 12 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau (CIB) have arrested a suspect previously wanted in connection to a Mississauga shooting. On Feb. , Police responded to a shooting at a plaza near Kennedy Road and Eglinton Avenue East which left a 19- and 21-year-old man seriously injured. Fortunately, both victims survived. The suspect was later identified as 22-year-old Carlos Rodriguez-Rodriguez of Mississauga and a Canada-wide warrant for his arrest was issued in May. Investigators later determined that he left the country following the shooting. On November 9, he returned to Canada and turned himself into police. He has been held in custody for a bail hearing and faces the following criminal charges: · Unauthorized Possession of Firearm · Knowledge of Unauthorized Possession of Firearm · Occupant of Motor Vehicle Knowing There was Unauthorized Possession of a Prohibited or Restricted Weapon Anyone with information is asked to contact the 12 Division CIB at 905-453-2121 ext. 1233.
